context: a letter from Edward Wilson, which you are answering
exchanges:
One of my correspondents in Australia writes me as follows in answer to the questions you propounded. I enclose you the extract from his letter to shew you that the matter has not been neglected.

I am dear Sir | yrs. faithfully | Edw Wilson

C. Darwin Esqre.

Many thanks for yr note. I recd a letter the other day from Dr Müller on the same subject, & from his kindness & yours, I shall receive more answer from Australia than from any other quarter of the world. This is a great piece of good fortune, as the Australians are I suppose nearly the most distinct of all races. This reminds me to ask you whether you happen to possess any moderately large photographs of Australians; In this case if you wd lend them to me for a day or 2 I wd send for them. I have a considerable collection, but it contains no Australian & I should like to compare them.

Pray believe me | yours very faithfully | Ch. Darwin
